report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Fixed deadline and budget provided, but scope is massively over-defined relative to constraints — this forces a predictive gate structure to surface the contradiction early

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build native iOS and Android mobile apps with real-time video streaming, offline sync, AI recommendations, social sharing, and in-app payments
project_understanding.trigger: CEO mandate to create a flagship market-disrupting product
success_definition: Both iOS and Android apps launched
supporting_quotes: Build a mobile app for customers
Full-featured native iOS and Android apps
The CEO wants this to be a flagship product that disrupts the market

patterns_detected.description: Input specifies solutions (native iOS/Android, VB6 backend, video streaming) without articulating the underlying customer problem these solve
2-week deadline + 1 junior developer + 1M concurrent users + zero downtime + 6 major features + legacy VB6 backend + $5k budget = mathematically impossible
Sole justification is CEO mandate ('disrupts the market') with no customer research, market validation, or business case

assumption_log.what: The project is intended for external customers, not internal use
assumption_log.why: Input states 'mobile app for customers' and 'flagship product' — standard language for customer-facing products. Internal tools are rarely described this way
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 13.2 — Stakeholder identification and requirements gathering
assumption_log.consequence: If this is actually an internal tool, the scope and success criteria change entirely. Scalability to 1M users becomes unnecessary; timeline and budget may be more realistic
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows risk analysis to proceed. Risks: if wrong, entire project classification and viability assessment is invalid

assumption_log.what: The 1 junior developer is the entire technical team — no backend team, no QA, no DevOps, no product manager
assumption_log.why: Input explicitly states 'Team: 1 junior developer' with no other roles mentioned. This is the only staffing information provided
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource estimation and team composition
assumption_log.consequence: If additional team members exist but were not mentioned, timeline and resource risk calculations are completely wrong. If this is truly a 1-person team, the project is not viable
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows staffing plan to be generated. Risks: if additional team exists, plan is wrong; if team is truly 1 person, plan is impossible

assumption_log.what: The VB6 backend is a hard constraint that cannot be replaced or modernized
assumption_log.why: Input explicitly states 'Must use legacy VB6 backend (cannot be changed)' — this is unambiguous
assumption_log.consequence: If the VB6 backend can actually be replaced or if a new backend can be built, the technical risk profile changes significantly. VB6 is not designed for mobile APIs or real-time streaming
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: clarifies technical boundary. Risks: VB6 + mobile + real-time streaming is a known-difficult integration pattern

assumption_log.what: The 2-week deadline (March 15) is a hard constraint that cannot be extended
assumption_log.why: Input states 'must be done by March 15' — language of a fixed, non-negotiable deadline
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 — Schedule baseline and constraints
assumption_log.consequence: If the deadline can actually be moved, the entire viability assessment changes. If it is truly fixed, the project is not viable with current scope and team
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows schedule risk to be calculated. Risks: if deadline is truly immovable and scope is truly fixed, project is not viable

assumption_log.what: The $5,000 budget is a hard constraint that cannot be increased
assumption_log.why: Input states 'Budget: $5,000 (very limited)' — explicit budget cap
assumption_log.consequence: If budget can be increased, viability changes. At $5k, this covers approximately 1 week of a junior developer's salary + zero infrastructure, third-party services, or testing tools
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows budget risk to be calculated. Risks: if budget is truly fixed, project is not viable

assumption_log.what: The 1 million concurrent users scalability requirement is a hard constraint
assumption_log.why: Input explicitly states 'Must support 1 million concurrent users' — no qualifier like 'eventually' or 'phase 2'
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.3 — Non-functional requirements documentation
assumption_log.consequence: If actual target is 10k or 100k concurrent users, infrastructure and architecture complexity drops by 2-3 orders of magnitude. Timeline and cost estimates change dramatically
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows architecture risk to be assessed. Risks: if this is a misunderstanding, entire technical plan is over-engineered

assumption_log.what: The 'zero downtime allowed' constraint means the system must support live updates without service interruption
assumption_log.why: Input states 'Zero downtime allowed' — standard language for high-availability requirements
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 — Quality requirements and non-functional specifications
assumption_log.consequence: If 'zero downtime' actually means 'minimal downtime' (e.g., 99.9% uptime), infrastructure requirements are less stringent. If it means true zero-downtime deployment, this requires blue-green deployment, load balancing, and database replication — all absent from current plan
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: clarifies availability requirement. Risks: zero-downtime architecture is complex and expensive

assumption_log.what: No formal stakeholder sign-off on scope has been obtained
assumption_log.why: Input provides requirements but no mention of stakeholder approval, requirements review, or sign-off meeting
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 13.2 — Stakeholder engagement and requirements acceptance
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholders have not formally approved this scope, requirements will change mid-project. If they have approved it, they understand the constraints and timeline
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows scope risk to be flagged. Risks: if stakeholders have approved, this assumption is unnecessary

project_plan.buffer_note: No buffer can be applied — deadline is fixed at 2 weeks. This is a critical risk signal

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Every single task is on the critical path with zero slack. A 1-day delay in any task causes the entire project to miss the deadline. One junior developer cannot execute 10 critical-path tasks in parallel

risk_register.description: If scope remains as defined (6 major features + 1M concurrent users + zero downtime) and deadline is fixed at 2 weeks with 1 junior developer, then the project will miss the deadline by 8-12 weeks minimum
risk_register.trigger: Project kickoff without scope reduction or team expansion
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Stakeholder must choose ONE of: (a) reduce scope to MVP (1-2 features only), (b) extend deadline to 8-12 weeks, (c) add 3-4 senior developers to team
risk_register.contingency: If deadline is immovable and budget is immovable, immediately escalate to executive sponsor and recommend project cancellation or complete scope reset

risk_register.description: If team is truly 1 junior developer with no backend, QA, DevOps, or PM support, then critical path tasks cannot be executed in parallel and the project will fail
risk_register.trigger: Confirmation that team is 1 person with no additional support
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Confirm actual team size and composition. If truly 1 person, add minimum 2 senior developers (1 iOS, 1 Android) + 1 backend engineer + 1 QA engineer
risk_register.contingency: If team cannot be expanded, reduce scope to single-platform MVP (iOS only) with basic features only

risk_register.description: If VB6 backend must be used and cannot be modernized, then integrating with mobile apps (iOS/Android) for real-time video streaming and offline sync is architecturally incoherent and will require significant custom middleware
risk_register.trigger: Confirmation that VB6 backend is truly immutable
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Clarify whether VB6 backend can be wrapped with a modern API layer (Node.js, Python, Go) that handles mobile requests. If not, project is not viable
risk_register.contingency: If VB6 is truly immutable and cannot be wrapped, recommend building new backend in modern language (Go, Node.js, Python) instead of using legacy VB6

risk_register.description: If stakeholder has not formally approved this scope in writing, requirements will change mid-project, causing further delays and cost overruns
risk_register.trigger: No written scope approval document mentioned in input
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Obtain formal written sign-off from CEO and all stakeholders on scope, deadline, budget, and team size. Document that they understand the constraints
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholders refuse to sign off on current constraints, escalate and recommend project reset with realistic parameters

risk_register.description: If budget is truly $5,000 and team is 1 junior developer, then budget covers approximately 1 week of salary + zero infrastructure, third-party services, testing tools, or deployment costs
risk_register.trigger: Confirmation that budget is $5,000 and is immovable
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Clarify actual budget. If $5k is truly the limit, project scope must be reduced to 1-2 features only, or budget must be increased to minimum $50k-$100k
risk_register.contingency: If budget cannot be increased, recommend project cancellation or complete scope reset to single-feature MVP

risk_register.description: If system must support 1 million concurrent users with zero downtime, then infrastructure must include load balancing, auto-scaling, database replication, CDN, and monitoring — none of which are mentioned in plan
risk_register.trigger: Confirmation that 1M concurrent users is a hard requirement
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Clarify actual expected concurrent user count. If truly 1M, budget must increase to $500k+ and timeline must extend to 6+ months
risk_register.contingency: If 1M users is truly required, recommend phased rollout: launch with 10k users, scale to 100k in phase 2, scale to 1M in phase 3

risk_register.description: If this is the junior developer's first mobile app project, first real-time streaming project, first offline sync project, and first AI integration project, then execution risk is extremely high
risk_register.trigger: Confirmation that junior developer lacks experience with any of these technologies
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Assess junior developer's actual experience level. If inexperienced in mobile development, add 1-2 senior mobile developers as mentors/leads
risk_register.contingency: If junior developer is truly inexperienced and cannot be supported, recommend hiring experienced mobile development team or outsourcing

risk_register.description: If project requires integration with VB6 backend, Apple App Store, Google Play Store, social platforms (Facebook/Twitter/Instagram), payment processors (Stripe/Apple Pay/Google Pay), and AI recommendation engine, then 6+ external dependencies create high integration risk
risk_register.trigger: Confirmation that all 6 integrations are required
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Confirm which integrations are truly required for MVP. Defer non-essential integrations (social sharing, AI recommendations) to phase 2
risk_register.contingency: If all integrations are required, add 1 integration specialist to team and extend timeline to 8-12 weeks

risk_register.description: If project includes in-app payments, then PCI DSS compliance, payment processor certification, and security review are required but not mentioned in plan
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Engage payment processor (Stripe, Apple Pay, Google Pay) early to understand compliance requirements. Add security review to Phase 3
risk_register.contingency: If compliance cannot be met in 2 weeks, defer in-app payments to phase 2 and launch with free version only

risk_register.description: If real-time video streaming must work with 1M concurrent users, then video infrastructure (encoding, transcoding, CDN, streaming servers) must be designed and tested, but no video infrastructure is mentioned in plan
risk_register.trigger: Real-time video streaming feature is implemented at scale
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Evaluate video streaming platforms (Twilio, Agora, Wowza) that handle infrastructure. Do not build custom video infrastructure from scratch
risk_register.contingency: If custom video infrastructure is required, extend timeline to 12+ weeks and add 2 backend engineers specializing in video

risk_register.description: If CEO expects a 'flagship product that disrupts the market' but timeline is 2 weeks and team is 1 junior developer, then stakeholder expectations are misaligned with reality
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Have explicit conversation with CEO about what 'flagship' and 'disrupts the market' mean given 2-week deadline and 1-person team. Reset expectations to realistic MVP
risk_register.contingency: If CEO insists on flagship product in 2 weeks, escalate and recommend project cancellation

risk_register.description: If 1 junior developer is assigned to 10 critical-path tasks with zero slack, then any illness, vacation, or context-switching will cause project failure
risk_register.trigger: Junior developer becomes unavailable for any reason
risk_register.mitigation: BEFORE planning: Assign backup developer to every critical-path task. If no backup exists, reduce scope to what 1 person can deliver in 2 weeks
risk_register.contingency: If junior developer becomes unavailable, project immediately fails — no contingency possible with 1-person team

project_viability.gap_amount: Timeline gap: 8-12 weeks past deadline (2 weeks available vs 10-14 weeks required). Budget gap: $45k-$95k over budget ($5k available vs $50k-$100k required). Team gap: 7 additional roles required (1 person available vs 8 required)

scoping_options.description: Reduce scope to single-platform MVP (iOS only) with 2 core features (basic video streaming + user authentication). Remove offline sync, AI recommendations, social sharing, and in-app payments. Extend deadline to 6 weeks. Increase budget to $15k. Add 1 senior iOS developer + 1 backend engineer
scoping_options.impact: Delivers a minimal viable product that demonstrates core video streaming capability. Can be launched in 6 weeks with 3-person team
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Sacrifices Android, offline mode, AI, social sharing, and payments. Does not meet 'flagship' or 'market disruption' expectations. Requires phase 2 for full feature set

scoping_options.description: Keep full scope but extend deadline to 12 weeks and increase budget to $80k. Hire 4 senior developers (1 iOS, 1 Android, 1 backend, 1 full-stack), 1 QA engineer, 1 DevOps engineer, 1 PM. Reduce concurrent user target from 1M to 100k for launch (scale to 1M in phase 2)
scoping_options.impact: Delivers full-featured iOS and Android apps with real-time video, offline sync, AI recommendations, social sharing, and in-app payments. Meets 'flagship' expectations
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Requires 12-week timeline (10 weeks past current deadline) and $80k budget (16x current budget). Requires hiring 7 additional team members. Concurrent user target reduced from 1M to 100k at launch

scoping_options.description: Recommend project cancellation or complete reset. Current constraints (2 weeks, $5k, 1 junior developer, 6 major features, 1M concurrent users) are mathematically impossible. Escalate to CEO and recommend either: (a) reduce scope to 1-2 features only, (b) extend deadline to 8-12 weeks, (c) increase budget to $50k+, or (d) cancel project
scoping_options.impact: Avoids project failure and team burnout. Allows realistic planning if project is to proceed
scoping_options.tradeoffs: Requires difficult conversation with CEO about unrealistic expectations. May result in project cancellation
